Harvest now, decrypt later is a 2026 procurement question rests on one claim: enterprises that industrialize measurement ship faster and defend it in audit. The pages that follow show the mechanics, not just the claim.

items: CBOM-grade discovery surfaces the shadow crypto nobody documented.
Crypto-agility architecture makes the next migration a configuration event.
Hybrid key establishment bridges the transition without waiting for perfection.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: We can describe exactly where Harvest now, decrypt later is a 2026 procurement question programs stall, because we have inherited enough of them: contract-less integrations, drift without owners and dashboards nobody alerts on. The pattern exists to prevent precisely these.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: NIST FIPS 203/204/205 turned PQC from research agenda into procurement requirement.
Where this shows up in our work

This perspective is grounded in Quantum Machine Learning & Simulation and Quantum Optimization for Enterprise Problems within the Quantum & Advanced Compute tower — each carried by our platforms with governance and evidence built in.
